title: What Is an LLM? Why Fluent Answers Aren't Proof of a Lookup | AI Terms in Ten Minutes
description:
How does a large language model (LLM) generate text? Why isn't a complete answer proof that information was actually found?
For people who use chat tools but often mix up models, data lookup and tool execution. No coding knowledge is needed.

We rerun three questions offline using six fictional lost-property records: an evidence-based lookup, missing data and a tool count. Six items total, four unclaimed, two unclaimed umbrellas; counts include their conditions and IDs. The story, chat bubbles and wrong answers are editorial illustrations, not actual outputs from any language model. The Python standard-library program makes no network or model calls. It verifies only data and counts, not model capability.

Six demo records: L001 umbrella / north counter / unclaimed; L002 water bottle / east shelf / claimed; L003 umbrella / west basket / unclaimed; L004 scarf / south hook / unclaimed; L005 hat / east shelf / claimed; L006 gloves / west basket / unclaimed. There are no owner-name or phone fields.
Actual offline output: looking up L001 returns north counter and unclaimed; asking for owner_phone returns UNKNOWN; unclaimed IDs are L001, L003, L004, L006; unclaimed umbrella IDs are L001, L003.

The three columns check an answer's evidence and execution records, not mutually exclusive abilities. Even with data or tool results, the final wording may still be model-generated. Leave unsupported parts unknown. If tools were used, check their conditions and actual results.

Full article and diagrams: https://mokaair.com/zh-TW/life/what-is-a-large-language-model
AI terms index: https://mokaair.com/zh-TW/life/ai-terms-index?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=ai-term-large-language-model

9n5m.text: Think of a text generator trained on many language patterns.

3wka.text: Input text is usually split into small processing units.

mjwt.text: Called tokens, they aren't always one Chinese character each.

gu98.text: There is no universal text-to-token count conversion.

tx7f.text: Dough is just an analogy here; we aren't counting text.

r75c.text: Common generative models use current input to produce the next token.

ba5g.text: The new output becomes input for the words that follow.

cvvb.text: The next token depends on prior text and generation choices.

m2hw.text: This is common causal generation, not every architecture.

c9pm.text: It cannot peek at text it has yet to generate.

kdby.text: Don't claim this means all language models work the same way.

k54b.text: Who refers to whom in prior text also affects this round.

5azz.text: In "she took his cup," the word "she" alone doesn't identify the person.

7yja.text: Common attention mechanisms use math to weigh input relationships.

gb26.text: They help process context and input relationships.

w4q8.text: They cannot guarantee every reference is correct.

jxrk.text: Ingredient amounts are an analogy; no baker lives inside the model.

4g2w.text: How do its learned abilities differ from the data you just pasted?

6wh6.text: Training shapes ability; this round's input supplies information.

58sy.text: A potter's practiced touch doesn't mean knowing every customer's cup.

zsri.text: Training adjusts many numerical values, usually called parameters.

fbw8.text: Parameters work together in calculations, not a searchable lost-property log.

caid.text: Training adjusts parameters; context is this round's available input.

kibv.text: Pasting data and retraining the model are two different things.

8gwq.text: New clay changes what you're working on this time.

d34y.text: Pasting the lost-item list supplies data; it doesn't retrain the model.

948s.text: A later chat sees it only if the system supplies it again.

g42q.text: Treat the model, current input and external tools as three roles.

kmr4.text: Asking for a table changes this round's task instructions.

c5rj.text: Asking to fill every field may yield data the source lacks.

q5ee.text: Ask: use only this list; mark unverifiable fields unknown.

ufjr.text: That's your requirement; still check whether it was followed.

q4ek.text: Stepwise generation is a mechanism, not a full reasoning ability test.

uuy8.text: Judge task completion by that task's results and standards.

cvde.text: Before testing models, can we run what this list actually establishes?

kcsa.text: Offline, we run three tasks: find a location, check a missing field, count.

d6ut.text: This proves the code counts by condition, not that any model is error-free.

y9ff.text: For a chat tool to do these steps, which other roles are needed?

x95w.text: A model can request a tool call; the program must send it for execution.

hwde.text: Asking a vendor to count stock won't make the boxes count themselves.

jb7z.text: The tool gets a request, handles data and returns results to the workflow.

77dr.text: Check the request: all records or unclaimed ones?

2sqz.text: Check execution: missing access or files may halt it midway.

kcrb.text: Check tool output; the model saying "I counted" isn't proof.

736v.text: If an empty-box query returns nothing, the model must not fill it in.

h7e9.text: It can put returned data into words, but may still omit conditions.

ucjp.text: The chat product you see usually includes more than just that text model.

8ppe.text: The model handles this input; the product handles data, tools and display.

zpm2.text: The same model may therefore do different things in different products.

hfed.text: Can it read your file? Check whether the product supplied its contents.

3qvj.text: Can it check stock? Check tool connections and what stock it can access.

w4hk.text: "Remembered" on screen doesn't mean the model's parameters were retrained.

g4ds.text: A product can save input and supply it to later chats.

xhwk.text: What it saves and when: check the product's instructions.

jh6k.text: The fluent vendor and stock-counting helper each still need checking.

ch7h.text: Request, output and final words must agree for this task to be complete.

zvsm.text: With data and tools, why might the final answer still be wrong?

hfmb.text: Trap one: fill nonexistent fields. Trap two: change the question's conditions.

5qgt.text: Six, four and two are in the same data, but answer different questions.

xa8z.text: Unclaimed items? Four: exclude those two claimed records.

9rgr.text: Trap three: repeat the question and treat repetition as independent evidence.

mbv2.text: Two identical texts may both repeat the same unsupported claim.

643y.text: We need sources, data and execution evidence, not just another answer.

ic9d.text: Check the source; missing fields stay unverified.

qd94.text: Check the same conditions; match each ID and status.

ntgg.text: Check whether results actually came back; keep failure messages too.

8duc.text: Even a source passage must support what you're actually saying.

e5ah.text: Likewise, model ability must be checked by task and criteria.

25k7.text: Now you know three traps. How can you check your next answer right away?

jmxp.text: Use three columns: generated text, then data and tool results.

7cws.text: No full architecture knowledge needed to split this into three jobs.

mf9z.text: Column one: generated text. Forming sentences doesn't prove facts.

megm.text: First identify words being organized; fluency isn't evidence.

zzw9.text: Column two: lookup. Name the record or source passage.

beye.text: Column three: tool counts. Conditions, execution and output must agree.

pvtj.text: Column two: traceable records. Match place and status to the source.

bj2g.text: Column three holds actual run results, not just "I've counted it for you."

2ctv.text: Leave any column without evidence unknown; don't fill it from another.

w9t3.text: Ask: use only this data; cite the supporting records.

eysm.text: Mark gaps unknown; say what data is missing.

t7h8.text: For counts, list conditions, actual results and traceable IDs.

ya9q.text: These three prompts don't guarantee truth. Open and check evidence.

vayd.text: If more data is needed, supply it; don't first demand more confidence.

yqvc.text: Tokens are processing units; context is input; training tunes parameter values.

daab.text: Separate model and context: do you need data or a different task?

pzcj.text: Retrieval finds material; tools process it. Their results still need checking.

zfi9.text: You need a verifiable task result, not an answer that sounds expert.
